title: Enlarge buffer cache and align planner I/O costs to cut physical reads
configuration_cause: shared_buffers=16384 (128MB) is far below the 2TB host RAM; blks_read_per_txn=1.51 vs blks_hit_per_txn=9.23 gives a low buffer hit ratio, and random_page_cost=4.0 overprices cached random reads, inflating physical I/O and terminal occupancy of GetUserTweets (88.5% of terminal capacity).
mechanism: The dominant transaction GetUserTweets consumes 88.5% of finite client terminal time at p50=196us, and the low_buffer_hit_ratio alert shows the working set is not retained: only 9.23 buffer hits per 1.51 physical reads per txn. Raising shared_buffers to 1GB retains more of the read-mostly working set, raising effective_cache_size tells the planner more pages are cached, and lowering random_page_cost/seq_page_cost plus raising effective_io_concurrency lets index-driven point lookups prefer cached paths and prefetch concurrently. Fewer physical reads shorten per-transaction service time, freeing terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
query_effect: Index and point-lookup plans for GetUserTweets/GetFollowers should favor cached index paths; physical block reads per transaction should fall while buffer hits rise.
expected_tps_effect: Increase: lower per-transaction physical I/O shortens GetUserTweets service time, freeing terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease in GetUserTweets p50/p95 as physical reads drop.

predictions.rationale: Larger cache plus cache-favoring planner costs reduce physical reads.
Fewer physical reads shorten dominant transaction service time.
Freed terminal capacity converts to more completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If the bottleneck is commit-path WAL sync rather than cache misses, the buffer bundle will not move blks_read_per_txn and TPS stays flat; a WAL-group action would be needed instead.
If only planner cost changes matter, effective_cache_size/random_page_cost alone shift plans without shared_buffers growth; blks_hit_per_txn stays flat.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent leaves 128MB shared_buffers on a 2TB host with a low buffer hit ratio and default planner costs that overprice cached random reads; the coherent cache bundle directly targets the dominant transaction's physical I/O.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: 1GB = 131072*8kB, 8x current, well within safe 8192-65536... capped at 65536 (512MB)
2x current toward host RAM scale, within 131072-1048576

knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost

nodes.label: Buffer cache capacity + planner I/O cost bundle
Higher buffer hit ratio lowers physical reads per txn

edges.relation: raises cache retention and cache-favoring plans
shorter service time frees terminal capacity
